71:1: God Almighty says: Indeed, We sent Noah - that is, Noah, son of Lamech - to his people, [saying], ‘Warn your people before there comes upon them a painful punishment.’ He says: We sent him to them, saying, Warn your people. The word an is in the accusative case according to some of the Arab scholars, and in the genitive case according to some of them. I have explained the reasons for each group of them, and the correct view in our view of that is what has preceded in this book of ours, which suffices without repeating it in this place. It is in the reading of Abdullah, as he mentioned: Indeed, We sent to his people, ‘Warn your people,’ without an. This is permissible because sending means saying, so it is as if it was said: We said to Nuh 71:Warn your people before there comes upon them a painful punishment. That painful punishment is the flood in which God drowned them.
71:2: And His statement: He said, ‘O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner.’ God Almighty says: Noah said to his al-Nas 114:O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner. I warn you of the punishment of God, so beware of it lest it descend upon you because of your disbelief in Him. Clear: I have made clear to you my warning to you.
71:3: And His statement: Worship God and fear Him and obey me, God Almighty says, informing about what Noah said to his al-Nas 114:Indeed, I am to you a clear warner, to worship God. He says: I am to you a warner who warns you and commands you to worship God. And fear Him, He says: And fear His punishment by believing in Him and working to obey Him. And obey, He says: And adhere to what I command you to do and accept my advice to you. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Worship God, fear Him, and obey me. He said: God sent the messengers to worship God alone, to fear His prohibitions, and to obey His commands.
71:4: And His saying, He will forgive you some of your sins, means: He will forgive you your sins. If someone says: Doesn’t min indicate some? It was said: It has two meanings and two places. As for one of the two places, it is the place where nothing else is appropriate. If that is the case, then it only indicates some, and that is like your saying, I bought from your slaves. In this place, nothing else is appropriate. Its meaning is: some. I bought some of your slaves, and from your slaves a slave. The other place is the place where it is appropriate, about. So if about is appropriate in its place, it indicates all of them. That is like your saying, My stomach hurts from food I ate. The meaning of that is: My stomach hurt from food I ate. And from is appropriate in place of from, and that is because you put about in its place, so the speech is appropriate, so you say, My stomach hurts from food I ate, and from food I ate. Likewise, His saying, He forgives you some of your sins is: He pardons you, and absolves you of them. It may be possible that its meaning is that He forgives you of your sins for which He has promised you punishment. As for that for which He has not promised you punishment, His forgiveness of them has preceded. And His statement, And He delays you for a specified term, means: He delays your terms, so He does not destroy you with punishment, neither by drowning nor anything else. For a specified term, means until the time He wrote that He will keep you for Him, if you obey Him and worship Him, in the Mother of the Book. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, for a specified term, he said: What has been written of the term, so when God’s term comes, it will not be delayed. And His statement, Indeed, the term of God, when it comes, will not be delayed, if you only knew, God Almighty says: Indeed, the term of God that He has written for His creation in the Mother of the Book, when it comes to Him, will not be delayed beyond its appointed time, and He will look after it, if you only knew. He says: If you knew that this was the case, you would have turned back to obeying your Lord.
71:5: God Almighty says: Noah said when he delivered the message of his Lord to his people, or warned them of what He had commanded him to warn them of, but they disobeyed him and rejected what he had brought them from Him, My Lord, I have called my people night and day to Your Oneness and worship, and I have warned them of Your might and power.
71:6: My call only increased their flight. He says: My call to them to what I called them to of the truth with which you sent me to them only increased their flight. He says: Except their turning away from it, fleeing from it, and turning away from it. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, But my supplication only increased their flight, he said: It has reached us that a man would go with his son to Noah and say to his son, Beware of this, lest he lead you astray. So I saw that my father had taken me to him and I was like you, so he warned me as I warned you.
71:7: And His statement, And whenever I called them to You that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, meaning, the Most High, the Majestic, says: And whenever I called them to anything except the acknowledgment of Your Oneness, and the obedience to You, and the disavowal of the worship of everything other than You, that You might forgive them if they did that, they put their fingers in their ears so that they would not hear My calling them to that, and they covered themselves with their garments, meaning: and they covered themselves with their garments, and covered themselves with them so that they would not hear My calling them to that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, They put their fingers in their ears, so that they would not hear the words of Noah, peace be upon him. His saying, and they persisted, means: they persisted in their disbelief and continued upon it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, and they persisted, he said: Persistence is their persistence in evil and disbelief. His saying, And they were arrogant with arrogance, means: They were arrogant and refused to submit to the truth and accept the advice I called them to.
71:8: He says: Then I called them to what you ordered me to call them to openly openly, not hidden. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Then I called them aloud, he said: aloud is speech that is spoken openly.
71:9: And his saying: Then I declared to them and whispered to them secretly, meaning: I shouted to them and shouted out what you ordered me to warn them with. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, that Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, said: His statement, I announced to them, he said: It is authentic. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid, I announced to them meaning: I shouted at them. His saying: And I confided in them secrets, means: I confided that to them in secret between me and them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And I confided in them secretly, he said: between me and them.
71:10: And His statement: So I said, ‘Ask forgiveness of your Lord, for He is ever Forgiving.’ He says: So I said to them: Ask your Lord for forgiveness of your sins, and repent to Him for your disbelief and worship of other gods besides Him, and declare Him One, and devote your worship to Him sincerely, and He will forgive you, for He is ever Forgiving of the sins of whoever turns to Him and repents to Him for his sins.
71:11: And His statement: He will send down upon you abundant rain, meaning: Your Lord will give you rain if you repent, worship Him alone, and sincerely worship Him. He will send down rain from the sky upon you abundant rain. Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: ‘Umar bin Al-Khattab went out to ask for rain, but he did nothing more than ask for forgiveness. Then he returned and they said: O Commander of the Faithful, we have not seen you ask for rain.’ He said: ‘You have asked for rain with the angels of the sky by which rain is sent down.’ Then he recited: ‘Seek forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving. He will send down upon you abundant rain.’ And he recited the verse in Surat Hud until he reached: ‘And He will add strength to your strength.’ (Hud 11:52)
71:12: And His statement: And He will provide you with wealth and children means: And your Lord will give you wealth and children, and He will increase them for you and increase what you have of them. And He will provide for you gardens means: He will provide for you orchards. And He will provide for you rivers from which you will water your gardens and farms. Noah said that to them, because they were, as he mentioned, a people who loved wealth and children. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then I called them openly… to his statement, and He will make for you rivers. He said: Noah saw a people whose necks were torn apart out of greed for the world, so he said: Come to the obedience of God, for in it is the attainment of this world and the Hereafter.
71:13: And His saying: Why do you not have reverence for God? The commentators differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: Its meaning is: Why do you not see God’s greatness? Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Why do you not expect for God awe? He said: greatness. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, Why do you not have reverence for God? He said: You do not see any greatness in God. Muhammad bin Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, the same. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, and Qais on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Do not have any reverence for God, he said: Do not care about God’s greatness. Abu Kuraib told us: Omar bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: Why do you not have reverence for God? He said: They did not care about the greatness of God. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Regarding His statement, Do not expect any majesty from God, he said: greatness. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, Why do you not have reverence for God? He said: You do not care about the greatness of your Lord. He said: Hope means greed and fear. Others said: The meaning of this is: You do not preach to God as He should be praised. Who said that? Muslim bin Junada told me: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Sami’, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Why do you not have reverence for God? He said: Why do you not glorify God as He should be glorified? Others said: Why do you not know God’s greatness? Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, What is the matter with you that you do not have reverence for God? He said: What is the matter with you that you do not know God’s greatness? Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Why do you not hope for a good outcome from God? Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, What is the matter with you that you do not have reverence for God? meaning a consequence. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Why do you not have reverence for God? He said: You do not have reverence for God. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Why do you not hope to obey God? Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God’s statement, What is the matter with you that you do not have reverence for God? He said: Reverence means obedience. The first and most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of this is: Why do you not fear God’s greatness? This is because hope is sometimes placed by the Arabs in a place of fear when it is accompanied by denial, as Abu Dhu’ayb said: If a bee stings him, he does not want to be stung by it and he opposes it in the house of the honeybees. What he means by saying he did not hope is: he did not fear.
71:14: And His statement: And He created you in stages means: And He created you in one state after another, sometimes as a drop of semen, sometimes as a clot, and sometimes as a lump of flesh. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And He created you in stages, meaning: a drop of semen, then a clot, then a lump of flesh. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And He has created you in stages. He said: From dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clot, then what was mentioned until his creation was completed. Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And He created you in stages. One stage as a sperm-drop, another stage as a clot, and another stage as bones. Then He covered the bones with flesh, then He created it as another creation, in which He caused hair to grow. So blessed be God, the best of creators. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And He created you in stages. He said: A drop of semen, then a clot, then creation, stage after stage. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: He created you in stages, that he said: From a sperm-drop, then from a clot, then from a lump of flesh. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And He has created you in stages, he said: A stage as a sperm-drop, then a stage as mixtures when the sperm-drop mixes with the blood, then the blood overcomes the sperm-drop, so it becomes a clot, then a lump of flesh, then bones, then the bones are covered with flesh. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, And He created you in stages, he said: A drop of semen, then a clot, little by little.
71:15: God Almighty says, informing about what Noah, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said to his people who were polytheists with their Lord, arguing with them with God’s proofs for His Oneness: Have you not seen, O people, so take heed, how God created seven heavens in layers, one above the other. Layering is a noun derived from their saying: It matched in layers, and what he meant by that is: how God created seven heavens, one heaven above another in layers.
71:16: And His saying, And He made the moon a light therein, means, And He made the moon a light in the seven heavens, and He made the sun therein a lamp. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Bashar told us: Muadh ibn Hisham told us: My father told us, on the authority of Qatada: Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers? And made the moon a light within them and made the sun a lamp? It was mentioned to us that Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As used to say: The light of the sun and the moon is their light in the sky. Read if you wish: Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers?... to the end of the verse. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, that he said: The faces of the sun and the moon are before the heavens, and their backs are before the earth, and I recite a verse from the Book of God about that: And He made the moon a light therein and made the sun a lamp. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And He made the moon a light therein, that He created the moon on the day He created the seven heavens. Some of the Arab scholars from Basra used to say: And He made the moon a light in them is said metaphorically, just as one says: I came to Banu Tamim, but it is only some of them who came.
71:17: God Almighty says: And God caused you to grow from the earth as a plant. He says: God created you from the dust of the earth, and created you from it as a creation.
71:18: God Almighty says: Then He returns you to it meaning: Then He returns you to the earth as you were dust, and He makes you as you were before He created you. And brings you forth a new coming forth meaning: And He brings you forth from it if He wills, alive as you were human beings before He returns you to it, and He makes you dust, a new coming forth.
71:19: God Almighty says, informing about what Noah said to his people, reminding them of the blessings of his Lord: And God has made the earth a carpet for you on which you can settle and spread out.
71:20: And His saying: That you may take from it paths that are difficult means: That you may take from it difficult, scattered paths. Fajaj is the plural of fajj, which is the road. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So that you may take from it paths that are wide open. He said: Roads and landmarks. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, That you may take from it paths that are wide open, he said: Paths. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, that you may take from it various paths, meaning: different roads.
71:21: And His statement, Noah said, ‘My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me,’ so they disobeyed My command, and rejected what I called them to of guidance and righteousness, and followed one whose wealth and children only increase him in loss, meaning: And they followed in their disobedience to Me one who called them to that, one whose wealth and children increased, but the abundance of his wealth and children only increased him in loss, far from God, and straying from the straight path. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, and his son. The majority of the reciters of Medina recited it, and his son, with the waw and the lam open, and they recited it like that in the entire Qur’an. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it with the waw closed and the lam still, and likewise everything that mentioned the son from Surah Maryam to the end of the Qur’an. Abu Amr recited everything in the Qur’an of that with the waw and the lam open except for this one letter in Surah Nuh, as he used to close the waw in it. The correct thing to say in this regard, according to us, is that all of these readings are well-known and have similar meanings, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.
71:22: And His saying: And they plotted a great plot, means: And they plotted a great plot. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, great, he said: great. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And they plotted a great plot, a lot, like His statement, They will hear therein neither vain talk nor falsehood. And great is big, as Ibn Zayd said: The Arabs say: A strange matter and wonderful with the light vowel, and wonderful with the heavy vowel, and a handsome man and good and beautiful with the light vowel and the heavy vowel, and likewise big and big with the light vowel and the heavy vowel.
71:23: God Almighty says, informing us about Noah’s statement about his al-Nas 114:And they said, ‘Do not abandon your gods, nor abandon Wadd, nor Suwa’, nor Yaghuth, nor Ya’uq, nor Nasr.’ These were a group of the children of Adam, according to what was mentioned about the gods of the people that they worshipped. And from their report, as far as we have been informed, is what follows: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Musa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays: And Ya’uq and Nasr It is said: They were righteous people from among the children of Adam, and they had followers who followed their example. When they died, their companions who followed their example said: If we made pictures of them, it would be more likely for us to worship them when we remember them. So they made pictures of them, but they did not die. Others came, and Satan crept up to them and said: They only worshipped them, and through them they were given rain. So they worshipped them. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: There were ten centuries between Adam and Noah, all of them Muslims. Others said: These are the names of the idols of Noah's people. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Do not abandon your gods, and do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwa’, nor Yaghuth, Ya’uq, and Nasr, he said: Wadd was for this tribe of Kalb in Dumat al-Jandal, and Suwa’ was for Hudhayl in Riyat, and Yaghuth was for Banu Ghatif of Murad in al-Jawf of Saba’, and Ya’uq was for Hamdan in Balkha’, and Nasr was for Dhu Kila’ of Himyar. He said: The people of Noah used to worship these gods, then the Arabs adopted them after that, by God, except for wood, clay, or stone. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Do not abandon your gods, and do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwa’, nor Yaghuth, Ya’uq, and Nasr. He said: These were gods worshipped by the people of Noah, and then the Arabs worshipped them after that. He said: Wadd was for Kalb in Duma al-Jandal, and Suwa’ was for Hudhayl, and Yaghuth was for Banu Ghataif of Murad in al-Jawf, and Ya’uq was for Himyar, and Nasr was for Dhu al-Kila’ of Himyar. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwa’, nor Yaghuth, nor Ya’uq, nor Nasr, he said: These were idols that were worshipped in the time of Noah. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Nor Yaghuth, nor Ya’uq, nor Nasr, that these are idols and were worshipped in the time of Noah. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, nor Yaghuth, nor Ya’uq, nor Nasr, that they are gods who used to be in Yemen. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, nor Yaghuth, nor Ya’uq, nor Nasr, he said: These are their gods that they worship. The reciters differed in their recitation of his saying wada. The majority of the reciters of Medina recited it wada with a damma on the waw, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra recited it wada with a fatha on the waw. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two readings known among the readers of the regions, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.
71:24: And His statement: And they have led many astray. God Almighty says, informing about what Noah said: Many people have been led astray by the worship of these idols that were created in the form of these people named in this passage. So the misguidance is attributed to the fact that their worshippers have been led astray by them, because they are the ones who lead astray. And His statement: And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error means: And do not increase the wrongdoers by their disbelief in Our verses except in error, except by a seal on his heart, so that he is not guided to the truth.
71:25: God Almighty means by His statement, because of their sins, that they were drowned. The Arabs make ma a conjunction in what is intended as a method of recompense, as one says: Wherever you are, I will be, and Wherever you sit, I will sit. The meaning of the statement is: because of their sins, they were drowned. Ibn Zayd used to say about this: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, because of their sins, he said, because of their sins they were drowned, so they entered the Fire. And the letter ba here is a separator in the speech of the Arabs. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, regarding his statement, Because of their sins they were drowned. He said: Because of their sins they were drowned. The reciters differed in their reading of his statement, from their sins. The majority of the reciters of the regions, except for Abu Amr, read it as from their sins with a hamza and a ta’. Abu Amr read it as from their sins with an alif without a hamza. We say that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. And His saying: So they will be admitted into the Fire Hell and they will not find for themselves besides God any helpers to exact retribution for them from those who did that to them, and not to prevent them from what was done to them.
71:26: And His statement: And Noah said, 'My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dwelling.' Dwellings means those who wander on the earth, going and coming. It is a verb from the verb 'to wander', 'dawwaran'. The 'ya' and the 'waw' came together, so the 'ya' preceded the 'waw' while it was silent, and the 'waw' was assimilated into it, and they became a double 'ya', just as it was said: 'Al-Hayy is the Qiyam from 'Qamat', but it is actually Qiyam, and the 'Arabs are standing, and there is no dwelling in it, nor Arab, nor noise, nor whistle, nor flame blower. By all of that he means: there is no one in it.
71:27: God Almighty says, informing us of what Noah said in his supplication to Him against his al-Nas 114:O Lord, if You leave the disbelievers alive on the earth and do not destroy them with a punishment from You, they will mislead Your servants who have believed in You, and turn them away from Your path, and they will not give birth to anyone but wicked ones in Your religion, disbelievers in Your blessings. It was mentioned that Noah said this saying and made this supplication after his Lord revealed to him, None of your people will believe except those who have already believed (Hud 11:36). Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller, By God, he did not pray against them until the revelation came to him from the heaven, None of your people will believe except those who have already believed (Hud 11:36). At that time, the Prophet of God, Noah, prayed against them, saying, “My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller. If You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not give birth to anyone but wicked disbelievers.” Then he made a general prayer, saying, My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house as a believer and the believing men and believing women... until His statement, perish. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Qatada recited: Leave not a single inhabitant of the disbelievers on the earth, then he mentioned something similar.
71:28: And his saying: My Lord, forgive me and my parents, meaning: My Lord, pardon me and cover my sins and those of my parents. And whoever enters my house as a believer, meaning: And whoever enters my mosque and my place of prayer as a believer praying, meaning: Believing in the duty that You have imposed upon him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr bin Adam told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of al-Dahhak, And whoever enters my house as a believer, he said: My mosque. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Sinan Saeed, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, similarly. And His saying: And for the believing men and believing women means: And for the men and women who believe in Your Oneness. His statement: And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction means: And do not increase the wrongdoers themselves with their disbelief except in loss. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, except for destruction, he said: loss. I have explained the meaning of the saying of the speaker: I have become innocent in what has passed with its evidence, and I have mentioned the sayings of the people of interpretation about it in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us: Muammar said: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: They used to beat Noah until he fainted. When he regained consciousness, he said: My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know.
